brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base with removable bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: Full hex bases piece:-1,0 / 0,0 / 1,-1 / 1,0 with bins bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 and bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 seated in their cells. Bins are configurator trays that drop into a cell; I did not test removal by hand.
Notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm, notch:0#-1,1#notch1) fills the empty position between bases (-1,0) and (0,0). Configurator accepted it; I did not visually confirm the drawer pulls out.
handle:0,0,0;top (addHandle) with three inserts, on covers over the triangle (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1). Configurator accepted it; I did not test lift strength.
Compact footprint of four cells plus a handle, but the print estimate is about 2453 g and 3532 min, and the configurator does not check weight or portability. Not verified.

finish.summary: Built a four-piece hex base (full bases at (-1,0), (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0)) with a notch drawer frame between (-1,0) and (0,0), two removable bins (a 3-compartment full-depth bin at (-1,0) and a 2-compartment full-depth bin at (0,0)), and a top carry handle on the triangle of covers at (0,0), (1,0) and (1,-1). Open faces are capped and joints are locked. Final check_build: ok, no issues, meshClash clear. Print estimate is about 2453 g and 3532 min, which is heavy for a "portable" organizer; that is a material/size tradeoff the user should review. No props were added since the brief is about the build, not its use.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
